requirements.evidence: Almost the whole contract is present: migration with unique (entity_id, email), cascade FK and reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_120000_create_entity_invites_table.php:17-38); EntityInvite model with HasFactory, enum/datetime casts, normalizing email mutator, scopes and entity() (app/Models/EntityInvite.php:12-81); factory with employee/7-days defaults, expired() and accepted() (database/factories/EntityInviteFactory.php:30-47); sendInvite implements validation, member/pending rejection, expired replacement, unique-race handling, per-manager/entity rate limit, queued mail, audit and reset (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:39-43,60-126); manager-only members page, invite list, detail modal with prefilled role, saveRole rules and confirm/cancel removal (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:56,142-223; resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:87-149); PendingInvites accept/decline with 403, expiry error, idempotency, firstOrCreate, session and redirect (app/Livewire/Entity/PendingInvites.php:14-101); queued markdown mailable and view (app/Mail/EntityInviteMail.php:13-38; resources/views/emails/entity-invite.blade.php:1-15); lang keys and pt_BR translations in both ui.php and pt_BR.json. Remaining gaps are edges: a foreign openMember() leaves a previous selection intact instead of selecting nothing, and decline() can delete an already-accepted invite.

conventions.evidence: Docs and changelog are updated (CHANGELOG.md, docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md), the migration has a reversible down(), mass assignment is deliberate (#[Fillable] at app/Models/EntityInvite.php:12), validation is server-side, Bulma and the existing <x-input> are reused, and sibling Livewire style is followed. The clear deviation is that the new domain writes are not Actions: invite creation and all its side effects live in Members::sendInvite (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:100-125) and membership creation on acceptance lives in PendingInvites::accept (app/Livewire/Entity/PendingInvites.php:34-48), whereas conventions require one app/Actions/* class per use case with authorization inside. Secondary: memberRole is validated with inline rules instead of a #[Validate] attribute (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:50,170-172).

security.evidence: Good baseline: every data-changing action resolves and scopes the record and authorizes it (Members.php:56,62,130,144; PendingInvites.php:93-99 for the invitee e-mail match), input is validated (Members.php:39-43,65-66,170-172), output uses {{ }} escaping, and #[Fillable] limits mass assignment. Gaps with limited impact: selectedMembershipId is a server-owned record ID without #[Locked] (Members.php:45), so a client can set it and call saveRole() without openMember(); closeMember(), confirmRemoval() and cancelRemoval() are public endpoints without $this->authorize (Members.php:154-159,193-201); and the action ID parameters are untyped, so an array payload can cause a 500 (Members.php:128,142; PendingInvites.php:14,65). None of these lets a non-manager write data because the entity scope and policies/guards still apply, but they violate the mandatory Livewire policy.

tests.evidence: Broad, meaningful coverage: model normalization/casts/scopes/cascade and mailable contract (tests/Feature/Entity/EntityInviteModelTest.php), both locales and theme (tests/Feature/Entity/EntityInviteMailTest.php), invite happy path, normalization, owner prohibition, quota, duplicates, expired replacement, unique race, employee mount denial (tests/Feature/Entity/InvitesTest.php), manager-only route, invite form, error-once, detail modal, foreign membership, draft role, owner immutability, last manager, removal confirmation/reset, cancel scoping and localized title (tests/Feature/Entity/MembersTest.php), and accept/decline/expiry/idempotency/403/onboarding divider/switcher (tests/Feature/Entity/PendingInvitesTest.php). Missing: the 'employees cannot send or cancel invites' test only asserts the component mount is forbidden and never calls sendInvite()/cancelInvite(); there is no denied-call test for confirmRemoval()/cancelRemoval() and no tamper test that directly sets the unlocked selectedMembershipId, and the foreign openMember test only asserts the exception, not that the selection stays empty.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly lean and reuse-oriented: EntityInvite::EXPIRY_DAYS is used by the component and factory, pending/forEmail scopes centralize invite queries, ASSIGNABLE_ROLES is shared, and managerCount()/inviteRateKey() keep removeMember and sendInvite small (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:27-34,242-252; app/Models/EntityInvite.php:20,61-75). Minor duplication: render() repeats the selected-membership eager-load/query that selectedMembership() already encapsulates (Members.php:231-233 vs 237-239); a few extra helpers/states (inviter, isPending, closeMember) are small and not heavy indirection.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods focused; non-obvious logic is commented (normalization before validation at Members.php:64, race handling at 108, entity scoping at 146, atomic claim at PendingInvites.php:35), and the code matches sibling Livewire components and the existing Blade style. sendInvite is long but linear (Members.php:60-126); no debug output or dead code; the duplicated selected query and two very similar modals are the only readability nits.

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: invite schema/model/factory/mail, Members rewrite, PendingInvites component and its two placements, lang keys, manager-only nav/dashboard links, invite cleanup alongside entity deletion, and the required docs/changelog updates. No unrelated refactors or features beyond the task.

issues.explanation: The new domain writes (creating an invite and creating the membership on acceptance) are implemented inside Livewire components, but the project requires one app/Actions/* class per use case with authorization inside, so these should be extracted (e.g. SendEntityInvite and AcceptEntityInvite).

selectedMembershipId is a server-owned record ID set only by openMember(), but it has no #[Locked]; a client can overwrite it and call saveRole()/re-render against another membership without going through openMember(), which violates the mandatory Livewire policy even though the entity scope and policy limit the impact.

closeMember(), confirmRemoval() and cancelRemoval() are public Livewire endpoints with no $this->authorize(...); they only toggle UI state and removal is re-authorized in removeMember(), but the policy requires every public action to authorize.

memberRole is user input but is validated with inline rules instead of a #[Validate] attribute as the project pattern prescribes; the rule should move to the property or a rules() method so it follows inviteEmail/inviteRole.

The action parameters ($inviteId, $membershipId) are untyped and not validated as integers, so a crafted Livewire payload (for example an array) can produce a 500 instead of a validation/404 response; validate or cast them before findOrFail().

If openMember() is called for a foreign membership while another member is already selected, findOrFail() throws before the method clears state, so the previous member stays selected instead of the required 'select nothing'; clear selectedMembershipId and the drafts before resolving, and assert that in the test.

decline() deletes the invite without checking that it is still pending, so a crafted call can delete an already-accepted invite and erase the acceptance/audit record; only pending invites should be declinable, or the accepted case should be a no-op.

issues.location: tests/Feature/Entity/InvitesTest.php (employees cannot send or cancel invites); tests/Feature/Entity/MembersTest.php (confirmRemoval)
issues.explanation: Unauthorized-call coverage is incomplete: the employee test only asserts the component mount is forbidden and never invokes sendInvite()/cancelInvite(), there is no denied-call test for confirmRemoval()/cancelRemoval(), and there is no tamper test that directly sets the unlocked selectedMembershipId.
render() repeats the selected-membership query already encapsulated in selectedMembership(); reuse the helper or a computed property to avoid the duplicated eager-load/query logic.
Both Bulma modals are plain divs without role="dialog", aria-modal or an accessible label, which conflicts with the project's accessible-markup convention; add the ARIA attributes.

review.summary: This change implements invite-only entity membership end to end: schema/model/factory/mail, a manager-only Members page with invite form and detail/removal modals, PendingInvites accept/decline on the switcher and onboarding, translations, docs and a broad Pest suite. The functionality is largely complete, but the new domain writes bypass the required Actions layer, selectedMembershipId is left unlocked and several public actions are unauthorized against the mandatory Livewire policy, with a few edge and test gaps, so it needs changes before merging.
